title: Khao Soi
subtitle: Thai coconut noodle soup
menu_blurb: A fragrant, rich coconut curry broth with crispy tofu, mushrooms, lemongrass and lime, coating every noodle. A true crowd pleaser.
intro: My son Max introduced me to this soup. The coconut broth is fragrant and rich, coating every noodle. It is crazy flavorful and a crowd pleaser!
origin: Khao soi hails from Chiang Mai in Northern Thailand, where the weather stays a bit cooler.

mise_en_place.label: Air fry
mise_en_place.task: Tofu, seasoned with salt and pepper and a light coat of cooking spray

mise_en_place.label: Slice
mise_en_place.task: Mushrooms finely, and julienne the bell peppers

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: An air fryer and a soup pot

items.name: Firm or extra firm tofu, sliced lengthwise about 1 inch thick
Baby bella mushrooms, thinly sliced and halved
Limes (one for the broth, one for garnish)
Shallots, finely diced (or half an onion)
Thai red curry paste (more for extra heat)

ingredients.note: Plant-based swap: use a vegan fish sauce.

items.name: Bean sprouts, cilantro or crunchy noodles, Thai basil, and lime wedges

prep_note: For the lemongrass, trim the woody top and stay away from the purple ring, then slice the rest and mince it finely.

steps.title: Prepare
instructions: Cut each vegetable and arrange each type on its own plate.

steps.title: Pre-cook
instructions: Cook the tofu in the air fryer, or lightly sauté it on both sides on a griddle.

steps.title: Make the broth
instructions: Have all of your ingredients in front of you.
In a large pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the shallot, garlic, and lemongrass and sauté until fragrant and golden, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook until softened. Add the red curry paste and spices and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk, broth, and lime leaves and bring to a simmer, stirring. Once gently simmering, add the fish sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and chili garlic sauce.
Add the tofu and simmer gently, covered. Avoid a high flame so the coconut milk doesn’t separate.
Add the peppers and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes.
Give it a generous squeeze of lime. Taste, adding more lime, salt, pepper, or curry paste as needed. Find the balance between salty, sweet, sour, and spicy.
note: Add more fish sauce, soy sauce, or salt, and make sure it is piping hot.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
instructions: Place the fresh noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, then rinse in cold water.

steps.title: Serve
instructions: Divide the noodles among bowls and ladle the hot soup over the top, which makes it easier to handle.
Garnish with bean sprouts, cilantro or crunchy noodles, Thai basil, and more lime wedges.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Add more soy sauce and chili to taste.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Add bok choy, and any mushrooms you enjoy.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Keeps well for days in the refrigerator, and it freezes beautifully.

notebook.question: What is tofu, and is it good for you?
answer: Tofu is a nutrient-dense, plant-based protein made from curdled soy milk pressed into blocks. It is a complete protein, containing all nine essential amino acids, and it is high in iron and calcium. It is generally considered very healthy: it supports heart health, may reduce the risk of certain cancers, and aids weight management. It is low in fat, cholesterol-free, and safe to eat every day.
Its nutrition varies mainly with firmness. Firmer varieties hold less water, so they carry more protein, fat, and calories per serving.

table.label: Extra firm
table.text: 15 to 17 g protein and about 145 calories

table.label: Firm
table.text: 8 to 10 g protein and 70 to 80 calories

table.label: Silken or soft
table.text: Higher in water, with about 4 to 7 g protein and 40 to 62 calories

benefits.label: Heart health
benefits.text: Cholesterol-free and low in saturated fat, tofu may help reduce LDL cholesterol. Studies show eating at least one serving a week may lower heart disease risk by 18%.

benefits.label: Nutrient-rich
benefits.text: A good source of iron, manganese, selenium, phosphorus, and calcium, especially when made with calcium sulfate.

benefits.label: Cancer risk reduction
benefits.text: Tofu contains isoflavones, which have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and potential protective effects against breast, prostate, and colorectal cancers.

benefits.label: Bone health
benefits.text: Its high calcium and magnesium content helps prevent osteoporosis.
